# midview-08-83 -- design workflow

**Read left to right. Each coloured group is one stage; edit only what is
on the canvas. Double-click a subgraph to see its plumbing.**

| stage | you edit |
|---|---|
| 1 REFERENCES | images in `ref-img/design/midview-08-83/zones/<zone>/` and `lighting/` -- no prompts |
| 2 PLAN + 3D | plan (Block Layout), HIDE PARTS |
| 3 FURNITURE BLOCKS | BLOCKS lines: place, size, `| prompt` per piece |
| 4 CAMERAS | numbers per camera, or CAMERAS FROM VIEWERS + orbit |
| 5 FIRST PASS | controls panel: seed, night, strengths, zoning |
| 6 INPAINT | a prompt per zone (+ on, denoise, seed); BLOCKS to redo |
| 7 OUTPUTS | nothing: `renders/design/midview-08-83_*` |

Muted: 8 PROPOSE BLOCKS (SAM 3.1 + MoGe), 9 BLOCK -> 3D ASSET (TRELLIS.2).

Built with `python tools/build_workflow_design.py plans/midview-08-83.yaml`.

## References

One folder per zone, one for the lighting. Drop images in; up to 12 per
folder are tiled into one sheet (4 across). No prompts here: each zone is
drawn from its own sheet, inside its own pixels only. The lighting sheet
conditions the whole frame, so the zones share one light.

A folder must hold at least one image.

Too literal (the reference's layout shows up)? Lower **REF RESOLUTION**
or **ZONE STRENGTH** in stage 5.

widgets_values:
## BLOCKS

```
name  x= z= w= d= h= [y=] [rot=] [shape=] [arot=] [asset=]  | prompt
```
- **x z** centre of the footprint, **w** along X (east), **d** along Z (south),
  **h** up; metres, origin = outer faces of the west and north walls.
- **y** base height (wall cabinets), **rot** degrees counter-clockwise from above.
- Drawn as a silhouette from its name (sofa, chair, bed, table, bench, shelf,
  cabinet, rug, plant; else a box) or `shape=`; it faces north (-Z) at rot 0.
- **| prompt** is drawn only on that block's pixels.
- An asset made in 9 replaces the box automatically; **asset=none** = box;
  **arot** turns the asset inside its box.
- Block Layout writes the lines to the plan's blocks file, which
  `build_massing.py` and the Admin Panel's Showroom Model page read.

Block colours in the block-ID pass follow line order: insert new blocks
at the end to keep the others' colours.

## Cameras

**By numbers** (default): each Create Camera Info is `look_at` -- the
eye position and the target, GLB frame (X east, Y up, Z south), metres,
and the vertical fov.

**By hand**: set **CAMERAS FROM VIEWERS** to true, orbit / pan / zoom
each viewer, Run.

**Top** is fixed and fills the fourth panel of the sheet: it pins the
layout for the other three.

Each camera renders depth, zone-ID and block-ID at 1664 x 928 (the strip
next to it, left to right).

## Models  (all in ComfyUI/models)

| folder | file |
|---|---|
| diffusion_models | `Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo-v0.3-6step-int8_convrot.safetensors` |
| text_encoders | `qwen3vl_8b_int8_convrot.safetensors` |
| vae | `qwen_image_2.1_vae_bf16.safetensors` |
| model_patches | `qwen_image_2.1_fun_controlnet_union_int8_convrot.safetensors` |

The turbo is the Qwen-Image-2.1 base with the Viggle v0.3 LoRA merged
in (Viggle/Qwen-Image-2.1-viggle-turbo). Its 6-step schedule needs a
resolution-dependent shift; the ManualSigmas nodes here hold it
pre-computed for each picture size (1664 x 928, the 2048 x 1152 sheet,
the 3072 x 1152 derive sheet, the 2560 x 1440 hi-res). If you change a
size, re-run `tools/build_workflow_fast.py` rather than editing them.

Sampler: euler + BasicGuider (no CFG, no negative prompt) -- the turbo's
rules. Refines use the last two nodes of the schedule (start ~0.7):
composition kept, detail re-drawn.

widgets_values:
## First pass

The four depth passes are tiled into one 2048 x 1152 sheet and sampled
ONCE, so every camera gets the same design. Each zone is conditioned by
its reference sheet inside its own pixels; the lighting sheet and the
day / night line sit underneath, over the whole frame; each block's
`| prompt` is drawn on its own pixels. A, B, C are then cut out,
upscaled and refined (last two turbo steps).

- **SEED** a new design for every camera.
- **ZONING** false: lighting references only (fast look-dev).
- **ZONE STRENGTH** how hard each zone follows its references.
- **LIGHT STRENGTH** the lighting layer underneath.
- **REF RESOLUTION** lower = looser, less copying of the references.
nodes.title: 5.0  First pass, how
which block prompts are in play
5.6  FIRST PASS  --  one sheet, four cameras

widgets_values:
## Inpaint

Each zone node redraws its zone in A, B and C: the zone's pixels
(from the zone-ID pass, grown and feathered) are re-noised and drawn
again from **your prompt + the zone's reference sheet**, depth locked;
everything outside the mask is kept exactly.

- **enabled** off: the image passes through (nothing is sampled).
- **denoise** 0.3 touch-up, 0.5 redraw details, 0.8 new design.
- **seed** the same for all three cameras, so they agree.
- **grow** pixels added round the zone (seams).

Zones run in order (1, 2, 3), then **BLOCKS** redoes the named
pieces (comma separated names from BLOCKS) with their own prompt.

## Propose blocks (muted)

Un-mute this group once `sam3.1_multiplex_fp16.safetensors` (checkpoints) and `moge_2_vitl_normal_fp16.safetensors`
(geometry_estimation) are installed.

For each render: SAM 3.1 finds every class in the list (`:N` = at most N
per view), MoGe estimates depth, the depth is aligned to the known room
(same camera, metric), and each find is back-projected and boxed on the
floor. Finds seen from several cameras are merged, whatever each called
them. Finds on an existing block are listed under `# already in BLOCKS`;
pendants and blobs over several pieces are listed as `# dropped`.

Copy the lines you want into BLOCKS (stage 3). Orange boxes in the
viewer are the proposals.

widgets_values:
## Block -> 3D asset (muted)

Un-mute this group once the TRELLIS.2 files are installed (README).

1. **ASSET BLOCK**: the block's name.
2. Block Crop Source picks the camera where that block is largest and its
   mask from the block-ID pass.
3. TRELLIS.2 (ComfyUI's own template chain) makes a textured mesh.
4. Mesh Into Block saves it as `model/assets/<plan>/<block>.glb`. From the
   next Run, Block Layout fits it into the block's box everywhere.

Best results: frame camera C close on the piece (three-quarter, from the
front) and set Block Crop Source `view` to 3. A piece that is 1 % of a
wide shot gives a blurry crop and a shallow mesh.

Front facing the wrong way? Add `arot=90` (or 180, 270) on the block's line.
